description: Resolve the base branch for a work branch from the [base] configuration.
given: a work-branch name, a [base] configuration, and — where the vector exercises the mode — the policy source and the base the invocation or the consumer configuration supplied
notes: Only valid configurations appear here. A `by_prefix` map with no empty-prefix default is a configuration error caught before the policy runs (Section 6.11), so it is a `validate_policy` vector, not a resolution vector.
The empty prefix is a prefix of every branch name, so longest-prefix-wins makes it the fallback without a separate rule.

`policy_source` is absent from a vector that does not exercise it, and such a vector is read under the default `policy_branch` (Section 8.1). Under `target_branch` the `[base]` section supplies nothing, because it sits in the document the base locates, so a vector for that mode supplies `base_branch` and the `base` table is present only to assert that it is not read (Section 6.4).

An invocation under `target_branch` supplying no base resolves nothing and is refused with `base_branch_missing` before validation. Which entry points require one is `requires_base_branch`'s question and is covered by `base-precondition.json`.

vectors.description: A branch matching no named prefix falls to the required empty-prefix default.
Two prefixes match; the longer one is selected (Section 6.4, longest-prefix-wins).
Prefix matching is over the branch name; `exp/` does not match `experimental/x` only because that name does not start with it, while `exp` would.
A work branch identical to a named prefix matches it.
A map carrying only the required default resolves everything to it.
Under `target_branch` the base is what says where host-side policy is read from, so it comes from the invocation or the consumer configuration and `[base]` is not consulted (Sections 6.4, 8.1).
A `[base] branch` in the located document does not become the base under `target_branch`: a branch named inside the policy cannot select the revision the policy is read from (Sections 6.4, 8.1).
`resolve` and `prefixes` sit in the same located document as `branch`, so `by_prefix` does not re-resolve the base under `target_branch` either; one invocation resolves one base (Sections 6.4, 12.4).

The exclusion is the mode's, not a change to the default: under `policy_branch`, with no base supplied by the invocation or the consumer configuration, `[base] branch` is still the lowest of the three sources (Section 6.4).
